content:
Maya: Taking over primary for the 07:00-19:00 shift. Quick summary from handoff page: there was a recurring spike in autocomplete latency for a subset of EU customers starting ~05:10 UTC. Ajay applied a temporary routing rule and we saw tail latency improve. Leaving notes and follow-ups here before I step in fully.

Ajay: Correct. Root cause looked like intermittent KV-cache invalidation on the kv-relay pool -> caused extra LM context fetches and slower responses for short completions (autocomplete flows). I switched EU traffic for the affected customers to the fallback model variant (gpt-small-quant) and forced a cache warm for the top 5 prefixes. Latency dropped from ~1.4s p95 to ~320ms p95.

incident-bot: PAGE: KV-RELAY-DEGRADED detected (alert id: 57233). Impact: ~0.8% of requests in EU had >1s latency. Pager sent to @Ajay @Maya. Links: https://ops.redwood/alerts/57233

Maya: Thx @Ajay. @Olivia can you confirm whether customer A's SLA window overlapped with the degradation (they reported slow suggestions)? Also @Leo, FYI on the routing change — please watch for any cache-thrash when we revert.

Olivia: Confirmed — customer A saw ~12% error/slow reports between 05:12-05:38 UTC. They use short prefix autocompletes heavily. I DM'd their SE to let them know we applied a mitigation.

Leo: Observed a small bump in egress CPU on the kv-relay pods right after the forced warm; added `kubectl top` snapshot in the incident log. No OOMs. Note: when we revert routing we should stagger rejoin to avoid evict storms.

Maya: Plan for my shift: 1) Keep fallback routing in place for now. 2) Run a controlled revert between 10:30-11:00 UTC with @Ajay and @Leo monitoring. 3) File follow-up tickets and schedule a short retro. If anything pages, I'll take primary and @Nadia will escalate.

Ajay: Runbook pointer I used: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-relay-cache-eviction — specific commands: ```bash
# force warm for top prefixes (careful, rate-limit)
curl -X POST https://internal-api/kv-relay/warm -d '{"prefixes": ["the", "to", "for", "re", "cli"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx'
# check cache hitrate
curl https://metrics.internal/kv-relay?panel=cache_hitrate
```

Maya: Noted. I also left a short diagnostic snippet in logs: ```text
[05:14:23] kv-relay-eu-3 ERROR cache_miss prefix="the" key=0x9af1a
[05:14:23] kv-relay-eu-3 INFO fetch-context duration=210ms src=blobstore
```

Olivia: Filing tickets now. I'll create: INC-7892 (customer impact & SE outreach), TSK-4421 (runbook gaps — we need clearer guidance on warm sizes), and ENG-OPS-121 (scheduling: staggered revert playbook). I'll link the incident log and attach the `kubectl top` snapshot.

Nadia: Heads-up: there's a 2-hour coverage gap tomorrow between 02:00-04:00 UTC where no secondary is scheduled due to a rotation overlap. Suggest we: A) move one backup to cover 02-06 UTC or B) swap shifts for that window. I'll put a calendar invite pending agreement.

Maya: Thanks @Nadia. That coverage gap is high risk given this morning's timing pattern. @Leo please propose a swap and I'll approve.

Leo: I can swap with @Nadia for the 02-06 UTC window — will update rotation and add to oncall-coverage doc.

Ajay: For the follow-ups, I'd like a short postmortem focusing on cache eviction telemetry: what thresholds triggered a mass eviction, why the warm didn't happen sooner, and whether our autoscaling transiently reduced capacity. Suggest owner: @Ajay + @Olivia.

Maya: Agreed. Action items captured: [1] Olivia -> create INC-7892 + link SE notes (due EOD). [2] Ajay -> reproduce eviction locally and add deterministic test (due 3 days). [3] Leo -> implement staggered revert script in infra repo (PR by next week). [4] Nadia -> update rotation calendar to cover gap (done by tomorrow morning). [5] Maya -> run the controlled revert at 10:45 UTC and monitor.

Olivia: INC-7892 created: https://tickets.redwood/INC-7892 — description + customer timeline attached. Also scheduled a 30-min retro for tomorrow 15:00 UTC (calendar invite sent to eng-oncall, eng-runtime, and customer-success).

Maya: I'll hold on the revert until 10:45 and postback here. If you don't hear from me by 10:50 assume I'm in the middle of mitigation and @Nadia escalate.

Ajay: Quick note: when we revert, use the `--drip=staggered` flag on the router patch to reintroduce traffic at 5% steps over 5 minutes: ```bash
redwood-router patch-route eu-relay --variant primary --drip=staggered --step=5 --interval=60s
```

incident-bot: REMINDER: Scheduled revert event at 10:45 UTC by Maya. Use alert channel `#eng-oncall` for monitoring.

Maya: Revert completed at 10:53 UTC. Observations: no significant latency regressions; small cache-eviction blip at 10:54 (p95 rose to ~480ms for 3 mins). Closed the temporary routing.

Leo: Verified traces and metrics — p95 stable after warm; marking follow-up tasks in infra board.

Olivia: Retro agenda: 1) timeline recap 2) runbook gaps 3) alert threshold tuning 4) rotation coverage fixes. Anyone want to add items?

Ajay: Add: telemetry improvements — emit eviction-rate metric per-pool and automated warm suggestion when eviction-rate > 0.2% within 5m.

Nadia: I'll post the rota update and ping the roster.

Maya: Thanks team. I'll close the thread after the retro. If anything else pops up, mention @Maya or @Nadia. :thumbsup:
